title: Sheafified presentation of modules of differentials
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings. The module of differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] $\Omega_{\mathcal B^\#/\mathcal A^\#}$ of the sheafified ring map is canonically the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $U\mapsto\Omega_{\mathcal B(U)/\mathcal A(U)}$, and the identification carries the sectionwise universal derivations to the sheaf universal derivation. Equivalently, both are the cokernel of the sheafified free-module relation map encoding additivity, Leibniz, and annihilation of $\mathcal A$ in the category of sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Here a derivation of sheaves is a morphism of underlying sheaves of sets satisfying additivity, the Leibniz rule, and vanishing on the image of the base ring on every object; the sheaf module of differentials means the representing module for this derivation functor, with its universal derivation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-differential-presheaf-relation-cokernel] to $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$. It supplies the explicit three-relation map $r:E\to F$, the presheaf $P(U)=\Omega_{\mathcal B(U)/\mathcal A(U)}$, and $p:F\to P$, $[b]\mapsto d_Ub$. In particular $Q=P^\#$ and $q=p^\#:F^\#\to Q$ form the cokernel of $r^\#$ in $\mathcal B^\#$-module sheaves. The site's smallness is part of the site convention in the statement; no flatness or sheaf hypothesis on $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ is needed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-sheafified-free-relation-comparison] to the same presheaf ring map. It gives $c_F:F^\#\cong\bar F=\mathcal B^\#[\mathcal B^\#]$ and $c_E:E^\#\cong\bar E$, normalized on the original generators, and $c_F r^\#=\bar r c_E$. Put $\bar q=q c_F^{-1}:\bar F\to Q$. The relation square gives $\bar q\bar r=q c_F^{-1}\bar r=q r^\# c_E^{-1}=0$, since $q r^\#=0$ by step 1. It is a cokernel of $\bar r$: indeed, if $h:\bar F\to N$ satisfies $h\bar r=0$, then $h c_F r^\#=h\bar r c_E=0$. Step 1 gives a unique $\alpha:Q\to N$ with $\alpha q=h c_F$, equivalently $\alpha\bar q=h$. This proves the common sheafified relation presentation asserted in the item.

source.place: Tag 08TP, lemma-differentials-sheafify; Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module; assembly of the three re-split inputs.

proof.text:
Use [lem-trf-sheaf-derivation-relation-representability] with $R_1=\mathcal A^\#$, $R_2=\mathcal B^\#$, $\psi=\varphi^\#$ and the cokernel $\bar q$ from step 2. It makes $d=\bar q i$ a universal sheaf derivation and gives the unique derivation-preserving isomorphism $e:Q\cong\Omega_{\mathcal B^\#/\mathcal A^\#}$ to any representing pair, as well as the cokernel map $e\bar q$. Write $d_{\mathrm{sh}}$ for the universal derivation of the chosen target, so $e d=d_{\mathrm{sh}}$. The generator normalization of [lem-trf-sheafified-free-relation-comparison] and the unit formula of [lem-trf-differential-presheaf-relation-cokernel] give, for $b\in\mathcal B(U)$,
$$d(\eta_{\mathcal B}b)=\bar q(i(\eta_{\mathcal B}b))=q(\eta_F[b])=\eta_P(d_Ub).$$
Applying $e_U$ gives $e_U(\eta_P(d_Ub))=d_{\mathrm{sh},U}(\eta_{\mathcal B}b)$. This is the asserted compatibility with each sectionwise universal derivation, and $e\bar q$ gives the target its same relation cokernel presentation.

lean.note: The sheaf differential module is expressed by its representing property among sheaf modules, using Mathlib Derivation' on the underlying presheaf. The unique isomorphism is normalized on the universal derivation and original sectionwise differentials. Helpers specialize existing free-module and sheafification functors; no alternative differential-module construction is introduced. The three free summands are encoded as the free module on their disjoint union.
